Clozapine monitoring CBC weekly 6 months, fortnightly 6 months, then monthly; psychiatrist only; agranulocytosis, myocarditis, seizures
Metabolic screening BP, BMI, glucose, lipids at baseline, 6 and 12 weeks, then annually; not dose-dependent; no labs for first-generation drugs
Outcomes 25% still on treatment at 18 months; under 10% chronic remission; under 15% first-episode remission at 5 years; antipsychotics reduce relapse
Psychosocial Family psychoeducation (relapse); ACT (hospitalisation in the severely ill); CBT (symptoms, uncommon); social skills training
New mechanisms Xanomeline-trospium: M1/M4 agonist lowering VTA dopamine, trospium peripheral; ulotaront: TAAR1 and 5-HT1A agonist, non-D2

Adverse drug reactions SLM01

Numbers ADRs 5–15% of drug management; antipsychotics 3× other drugs; 10% of drugs withdrawn or black-boxed in 25 years
WHO types A augmented dose-related, expected, most common; B bizarre host-dependent (all Gell and Coombs); C chronic dose- and time-related; D delayed; E end of use (increase the dose); F failure
Gell and Coombs I minutes IgE anaphylaxis; II minutes–hours IgG cytopenias; III hours IgG serum sickness; IV days T cells rash
Four strategies · four severities Watch and wait; change dose and monitor; discontinue; continue and add · mild, moderate, severe (stop + treat + medical attention), lethal
Reporting Hospital under Vanessa's Law; individual: new drugs under 5 years, bizarre, severe or lethal
Prescription rules No trailing zero, always a leading zero, never OD/QD/QOD/U, state the route
Serotonin syndrome Triad neuromuscular excitation, altered mental status, autonomic; 28% within 1 h, 61% within 6 h; under 12 h abrupt; hyperreflexia, clonus, mydriasis, hyperactive bowels; moderate under 40 °C, severe at or above
Serotonergic mechanisms Uptake: SSRI, SNRI, TCA, tramadol, dextromethorphan, methadone, St. John's Wort; breakdown: MAOI, linezolid; release: amphetamine; precursor: tryptophan; PK: CYP inhibitors
NMS Incidence 0.01–0.2%; mental status change first, then rigidity, autonomic instability, hyperthermia; 1–3 days; hyporeflexia, normal pupils; 6–10% fatal; 30% rhabdomyolysis; D2 blockade
Case One citalopram tablet on St. John's Wort and L-tryptophan: severe Type A pharmacodynamic interaction; stop all three

Personality disorders and validation PD workshop

Exam scope Memorise borderline criteria only; others by gestalt; narcissistic and borderline asked most
Not mild Functioning like schizophrenia; 12–20 years lost; ICD dimensional but kept BPD
Validation is Expressing what makes sense in the other's experience; lowers arousal; BPD develops from invalidation
Validation is not Praise, questions (a change strategy), problem-solving
Five levels Appear interested; simple reflection; tentative mind reading (anger hides fear); makes sense given history; makes sense for anyone (best). Slide lists six with genuineness
Rules Validate the emotion not its size or the belief; emotions always valid; “and” not “but”; disappointment not warmth after self-harm
Cluster A Schizotypal odd beliefs and illusions; schizoid negative symptoms only; schizophrenia full delusions and hallucinations

Child psychiatry Klein

Numbers 20% of children; 70% of adult illness begins before 18; peak onset 15, 75% by 25; 1 in 5 get care
Interview Together, child alone, parents alone, together; 0–6 play, 7–11 dialogue, 12–18 with and without parents; 9-year-old “not wanting to be alive”, 15-year-old “suicidal thoughts”
Milestones Smile 6 wk, roll 3 mo, sit 6 mo, crawl 6–9 mo, walk and first words 12–18 mo, two words 2 y, tricycle 3 y
Additions Strengths in the history; parent-child interaction in the MSE; HEADSS; three wishes
Management Safety, investigations (collateral, PHQ-9, GAD-7, SNAP-IV, bloods with ferritin, TSH, B12), meds, therapy, school, community, other
Law Confidentiality limits: self, others, children under 16, driving. No minimum age of consent; understand and appreciate, presumed. Report under 16 on suspicion, personally, again on new grounds; 16–17 permitted
Anxiety Most common; 7% globally, median onset 11, lifetime 20–30%; separation, phobia, social, generalised; youth GAD 1 of 6; selective mutism 1 month; school avoidance not a diagnosis
Depression Irritable mood counts; youth dysthymia 1 year; over 60% comorbid; lifetime 11%, 20% by 18, 60% recur by 21; SI 5.5% M, 10.7% F
Mimics Anxiety: hyperthyroidism; depression: hypothyroidism
Treatment CBT gold standard, IPT-A; SSRIs off-label in Canada for impairment or poor CBT progress; FDA black box: observe for suicidality to 24
Attachment Bowlby bond with primary caregivers; Strange Situation reunion; anxiety × avoidance grid; disorganised high on both; siblings are not attachment
ACEs Felitti 7 categories, 9,508 respondents, dose-response; CDC 10 items 3+2+5; pyramid via epigenetics and adaptations to early death; toxic stress at the far right
Social media 95% of teens; over 3 h/day doubles risk; 30 min/day × 3 weeks improves depression; girls and the already unwell most at risk

ADHD SLM02 · CADDRA 2024

Criteria Often; 6 months; 2 settings; before 12; 6 of 9 (5 at 17+); 5–8% youth, 2–4% adults
Missed in adults Hyperactivity internalises; women internalise; IQ and hyperfocus compensate; transitions unmask (loss of structure first)
Comorbidity Depression episodic vs ADHD continuous; anxiety, especially in women, mitigated by treating ADHD; 55% in the 95th percentile of emotion dysregulation; substance use even controlling for amount; SSRI fogging
Screening Interview, collateral, MSE; ASRS Part A ≥4 of 6 positive, rules out better than in; CADDRA checklist childhood and current on one form (onset before 12)
Treatment order Psychoeducation first; strategies (exercise 1 h → 4 h focus, body doubling, gamification, Pomodoro 25/5 flags wear-off, visual Eisenhower, sequential reminders); CBT 67 vs 33%, 53 vs 28%; then a long-acting stimulant
First line Adderall XR, Vyvanse (prodrug, max 60), Biphentin (adult max 80), Concerta (OROS, adult max 72), Foquest, Quillivant
Second line Short-acting stimulants; atomoxetine (NRI, 24 h, 0.5 → 1.2 mg/kg, max 100 mg); guanfacine XR (α-2A, 1 mg, max 4 mg at 6–12, 7 mg at 13–17)
Mechanisms Amphetamine inhibits VMAT2 and reverses the transporter; methylphenidate blocks DA and NA reuptake; atomoxetine NA reuptake; guanfacine prefrontal α-2A
Before a stimulant Take it early, after food; lunch alarm; caffeine compounds, alcohol stronger, cannabis blunts

Skull, meninges, sinuses Lisk · Lab 10

Bones and sutures 8: frontal, 2 parietal, 2 temporal, occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid. Coronal frontal-parietal, sagittal, lambdoid, squamous; bregma anterior fontanelle, lambda posterior
Pterion Frontal, parietal, squamous temporal, greater wing; thinnest; middle meningeal beneath via foramen spinosum → epidural
Arteries in Internal carotid via carotid canal; vertebrals via foramen magnum; middle meningeal via foramen spinosum; brain = internal carotid + vertebral, dura = external carotid
Fossae Anterior frontal lobes; middle temporal lobes and pituitary (sphenoid floors it, carries rotundum, ovale, spinosum); posterior cerebellum and brainstem
Meninges Dura periosteal + meningeal; arachnoid avascular, bridges sulci; pia adherent, dips in. Cranial epidural potential, spinal epidural real; subdural potential; subarachnoid real, CSF
Partitions Falx cerebri (longitudinal fissure, crista galli); tentorium (transverse fissure, petrous ridge anteriorly, occipital posteriorly; midbrain in the notch); diaphragma sellae; falx cerebelli (lab)
Compartments Supratentorial: hemispheres, diencephalon, CN I–II; infratentorial: brainstem, cerebellum, CN III–XII
Drainage SSS → confluence → transverse → sigmoid → jugular foramen → IJV; ISS + great cerebral vein → straight → confluence; cavernous → superior petrosal (transverse) or inferior petrosal (IJV)
Cavernous sinus Wall top-down III, IV, V1, V2; lumen carotid + VI (first to fail); danger triangle via ophthalmic veins and pterygoid plexus, valveless
Fractures Otorrhagia = temporal bone; child fracture = straight, sharp, non-serrated, wrong place; both paediatric cases parietal

Brain, ventricles, imaging Lisk · Moreland · Lab 10

Development Three vesicles at 4 weeks: prosencephalon (telencephalon hemispheres, diencephalon thalamus), mesencephalon, rhombencephalon (metencephalon pons + cerebellum, myelencephalon medulla)
Lobes Central sulcus frontal/parietal; lateral fissure temporal; parieto-occipital; insula deep to lateral fissure; limbic = cingulate, parahippocampal, uncus; six (lab), five (lecture)
Functional Precentral motor, postcentral sensory; language left in most; contralateral control
Grey and white Cord: horns inside, columns outside; forebrain: cortex outside plus deep nuclei, white matter deep
Fibres Commissural (corpus callosum genu, body, splenium; forceps minor frontal, major occipital; anterior commissure); projection (corona radiata, internal capsule: posterior limb corticospinal); association
CSF Choroid plexus → lateral ventricles → Monro → third (thalamus) → Sylvius (midbrain) → fourth → Magendie (median) + Luschka (lateral) → subarachnoid, cisterns → granulations → SSS
Cisterns Interpeduncular in front of midbrain; ambient around; superior behind under splenium; cisterna magna cerebellum-medulla
Monro-Kellie Brain, blood in vessels, CSF, other; mass effect and herniation are the concern in everything
Modalities CT first (bone, acute blood); MRI problem-solving (parenchyma; poor for bone); contrast for vessels, inflammation, lesions; ultrasound only in neonates; CT facial bones separately
Haemorrhages Epidural: middle meningeal, arterial, lens, stops at sutures, fracture. Subdural: bridging veins, crescent, crosses sutures, elderly. Subarachnoid: sulci and cisterns, aneurysm, angiography. Parenchymal: hypertension, trauma, infarct, tumour, amyloid
Hydrocephalus Obstructive: upstream ventricles only (aqueduct: lateral + third, fourth normal); non-obstructive: granulations blocked, all dilate (post-SAH)
Herniation Subfalcine (midline shift), central, uncal (blown pupil), transcalvarial, upward cerebellar, tonsillar; low pressure from a CSF leak also drops the tonsils
Masses and infection Intra- vs extra-axial (meningioma: CSF rind); small lesion, huge oedema = metastasis; large tumours can hide on non-contrast CT; metastasis, abscess, glioblastoma may be indistinguishable; cascade meningitis → cerebritis → ventriculitis (FLAIR; kills via hydrocephalus) → abscess (T1 + contrast)
Imaging extras Three H's: herniation, hydrocephalus, haemorrhage. Bright = clot: coagulopathic bleeds can be isodense. Hypertensive bleed = basal ganglia. Epidural kills fastest, subdural hardest to stop. Gas under a fracture → open, barrier-crossing antibiotics early. Clear nasal drip = CSF via cribriform plate. Depressed vertex fracture → superior sagittal sinus. Blood causes both hydrocephalus types

Interview, MSE, appraisal CS2 · HSR

Hierarchy Physical/drug (confusion) → psychosis (impaired reality-testing) → mood and anxiety; work top down

Formulation Taylor: classify the illness, discern the predicament, discover the disease; plan biopsychosocial, feasible, safe; 2–3 sentence summary then impression
Critical appraisal Useful and relevant to this patient; EIP: evidence, resources, clinical state, patient preferences, expertise integrates; pyramid filtered above unfiltered
CASP Ten checklists; valid, results, relevant; cohort A/B/C, RCT A+B/C/D
Papers Tiihonen 2017 cohort of 29,823 (Finnish register); Lieberman 2005 RCT (CATIE); chronic-schizophrenia population fits the family-practice case, not the substance-induced one
